newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Portuguese oppose olive oil reform.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese oppose olive oil reform.

text.p: A plan to reform the European Union's olive oil regime by paying aid per tree was opposed by Portugal at Monday's farm ministers meeting, an EU official said.
"The Portuguese said during a brief discussion that the option to pay aid per tree would encourage producers not to harvest their crops," the official explained.
Farm Commissioner Franz Fischler outlined a discussion paper to ministers which sets out two alternative reform measures.
Ministers referred the issue back to the special committee on agriculture after Fischler said that he hoped to put forward a proposal before the summer.
Last week Fischler told a news conference that he favoured paying aid on a per-tree basis because it would be simpler to control than counting olives.

He said that he doubted that producers would abandon their crops because olives would still be worth money. The discussion paper's second option would maintain the current regime and reduce the risk of fraud by introducing national production thresholds.
He told the news conference that he planned to introduce a formal proposal in time for the 1998 season which begins in November.
